spans.s:
Kaiśinī.--The Kaiśinyaḥ prajāḥ, ‘offspring or people of keśin,’ are mentioned in an obscure passage of the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa either as still existing at the date of the brāhmaṇa or as extinct.
Foot notes So Sāyaṇa.
xi. 8, 4, 6.
Cf. Eggeling, Sacred Books of the East, 44, 134.
Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 208.

Kaiśorya, ‘descendant of Kaiśori,’ is the patronymic of kāpya in the first two Vaṃśas (lists of teachers) in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad.
Foot notes ii. 5, 22; iv. 5, 28 (Mādhyaṃdina = ii. 6, 3; iv. 6, 3 kāṇva).
